Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back. Bangladesh are in a huddle before they spread onto the field. Out come the West Indies openers - Brandon King and Johnson Charles in pursuit of a huge score. Taskin Ahmed will start with the ball for the visitors. Here we go!
…THE RUN CHASE…
Right then, the West Indies need to chase a record score of 190 to salvage some pride in the series. Can they do it or will Bangladesh make a clean sweep? Join us in a bit for the second essay.

Roston Chase is in for a chat. He says that the wicket is a lot better tonight. Feels that they have conceded a few runs too many but he backs the team to chase this down. Shares that Akeal Hosein is a vital player and not having him is a loss but cricket is a team sport and others must step up in his absence.

West Indies were below par with the ball and sloppy on the field. Romario Shepherd was the pick of the bowlers with 2/30 in his spell while Roston Chase and Motie also did a fair job. The home side leaked plenty of runs in the back half of the innings and this might come to bite them.

25 runs from the final over propel Bangladesh to their highest score of the series by a far margin as they finish with 189/7 in their 20 overs. Opting to bat first, Bangladesh got off to a powerful start with Parvez Hossain Emon and Litton Das who added 44 inside the first five overs. Emon was the aggressor of the duo with 39 off just 21. A couple of wickets fell in quick time before Mehidy Hasan and Jaker Ali added a handy 37-run stand. Mehidy departed on 29 but Jaker Ali carried on and smashed an unbeaten 72 off 41 to take his side toward the 190-run mark.

OUT! RUN OUT! Would you believe it? The second run out of the over and Mahedi Hasan goes without facing a ball. This is flat and short, on off, Jaker punches it firmly to the left of backward point and sets off for a tight single as does Mahedi. Mahedi is struggling to make his ground at the batting end as Rovman Powell is quick to get to his right and releases it while on the run. The throw is accurate just behind the stumps at the batting end. Nicholas Pooran collect it cleanly and the replays that Mahedi is short of his ground despite the dive.

OUT! RUN OUT! A massive mix-up and Shamim Hossain is gone! Attacking the stumps, on a nagging length, Jaker drops it with soft hands in the square leg region and calls two immediately. They take the first run comfortably and both are caught ball-watching while going for the second run as the keeper Nicholas Pooran gets to the ball quickly by running to his left. Both batters are at the same end as the throw from Pooran goes to the bowling end. Chase stays beside the stumps and does the rest. Jaker is fuming as he trudges off. Now then - Jaker is already back in the pavilion but the third umpire is called into action to check which of the two batters is out. The replays show that Shamim failed to retreat and get back inside the crease at the batting end. His bat was in the air and by the time, he could ground his bat in, Jaker crossed Shamim and therefore, it will be Shamim who will be deemed out. Quite remarkable scenes!

Commentary.Commentary: All set for the action to start. The two umpires and players head out to the centre. It will be Litton Das and the debutant Parvez Hossain Emon to open the innings for Bangladesh. One of two debutants for West Indies, Jayden Seales will start with the new ball. A slip in place. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Nikhil Uttamchandani and Carlos Brathwaite are near the deck. Nikhil informs that a nice breeze is blowing from the east and if it continues to do so, we may not see any dew formation. Feels that the batters will have to take wind into account while going for the big shots. Carlos mentions that this is the same surface which was used in the first game. Adds that there's very little grass and it will mean that the pitch will be on the drier side, making run-scoring a challenge.

Nicholas Pooran is up for a chat. He says that it's all about taking responsibility but they have rushed a bit. Shares that he tries to bat deep after getting into his innings. Adds that he wants to get a good score and keep improving as a batter. Ends by sharing that he is trying to prioritize and play as long as possible and is looking forward to finishing the year with a win.

Rovman Powell, the West Indies skipper says that they haven't played good cricket. Adds that they have lost the series but want to end it on a high and put up a better show for the fans. Shares that they have two debutants - Justin Greaves and Jayden Seales in place of Andre Fletcher and Akeal Hosein.

Litton Das, the Bangladesh skipper opts to bat first. He says that the wicket looks good for batting and they want to defend as they did in the first two matches. Adds that he is happy to lead this side. Shares that they have won the series but they want to win the final game and complete a whitewash. Ends by sharing that Parvez Hossain Emon is playing in place of Soumya Sarkar as their only change and they aren’t risking Nahid Rana because of his workload.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Brandon King, Johnson Charles, Nicholas Pooran (WK), Roston Chase, Rovman Powell (C), Justin Greaves (in place of Andre Fletcher) (On T20I debut), Romario Shepherd, Gudakesh Motie, Alzarri Joseph, Obed McCoy, Jayden Seales (in place of Akeal Hosein) (On T20I debut).

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Litton Das (C/WK), Tanzid Hasan, Parvez Hossain Emon (in place of Soumya Sarkar) (On T20I debut), Mehidy Hasan, Jaker Ali, Rishad Hossain, Mahedi Hasan, Shamim Hossain, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, Taskin Ahmed, Hasan Mahmud.
Toss Update - Bangladesh have won the toss and opted to BAT first.
Team News - Akeal Hosein will miss the final T20I for the West Indies with franchise commitments while Soumya Sarkar has been ruled out of this fixture for Bangladesh with a broken finger.

On the flip side, Bangladesh have been extremely good in the first two games. They batted first again in the second match of the series and posted a fighting score of 129 with runs from Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Jaker Ali, and an important cameo from Shamim Hossain. All the bowlers collectively stepped up with Taskin Ahmed leading the way in defence of a low score and they successfully did it, winning by 27 runs. Bangladesh will be raring to make the scoreline 3-0 and end their tour on a high. So, can the West Indies bounce back, or will Bangladesh make a clean sweep? We shall find out soon. Toss and team news in a bit. Stay tuned!

West Indies were favorites to win the series but have had a couple of poor batting efforts that have disappointed them. They bowled first and had better conditions while batting but have thrown their wickets away to poor shots. Their bowlers did an excellent job in game two to keep the visitors under 130 with both the left-arm spinners doing an outstanding job. Chasing the score, the Men in Maroon were reduced to 42/6. Roston Chase and Akeal Hosein made handy 30s but they were eventually dismissed for just 102 runs. Standing on the brink of a whitewash, the home side will need to step up and end the series with a win.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the third and final T20I of the series between the West Indies and Bangladesh from the Arnos Vale Stadium in St Vincent. After two impressive wins, the visitors have already sealed the series and will look to make a clean sweep while the West Indies will hope to salvage some pride with a consolation win.
...MATCH DAY...

After a rollercoaster series, the West Indies’ hopes of remaining unbeaten across all formats have been dashed. The Test series ended 1-1, and while the Windies dominated Bangladesh with a 3-0 whitewash in the ODIs, the tables have turned in the T20Is. The visitors have already clinched the series 2-0 with one game to spare, handing the hosts a bitter lesson in resilience and consistency. Chasing modest totals has exposed the cracks in the Windies’ batting lineup. Despite having explosive hitters like Johnson Charles, Andre Fletcher, and Nicholas Pooran - who leads the charts for most sixes in T20s this year - it was Roston Chase and Akeal Hosein who top-scored in the second match. That’s a worrying sign for the home side. On the brighter side, the bowling attack has been a revelation. Alzarri Joseph, Obed McCoy, and Romario Shepherd have been exceptional with pace, while Gudakesh Motie’s left-arm spin has kept the opposition on their toes. For Bangladesh, this series has been all about grit and determination. Winning the first two matches from tough situations shows how far they’ve come. Shamim Hossain has stepped up as a dynamic finisher, delivering crucial runs down the order. Mehidy Hasan and Jaker Ali have been consistent rocks in the middle order, while skipper Litton Das is due for a big contribution. However, they will miss the services of Soumya Sarkar in this game which could give an opportunity to Tanzid Hasan or Parvez Hossain Emon to shine at the top. The bowling attack has been sharp, with Taskin Ahmed, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, and Hasan Mahmud forming a potent pace trio, complemented by Mahedi Hasan’s six wickets with his clever spin. As we head into the final showdown, the stakes are high. Will Bangladesh seal an emphatic 3-0 sweep and roar with pride? Or will the Windies rally to salvage some honor in front of their home fans? We will find out soon.
